# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly, claiming to have remained continuously in her teenage years.  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** Widowed  <sub>[v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059), [v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for Tabby's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face, rose-colored cheeks, and silver-white hair arranged in charming small rolls above her ears. She has large, tender blue eyes with an irrepressible youthfulness and an expression full of expectation.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia describes herself as outmoded in her garments and views, yet she holds an indulgent, relaxed attitude toward the young women in her charge and refuses to police their conduct. She enjoys continuous laughter and maintains a cheerful outlook on life, believing in fulfilling her obligations while enjoying her days. She holds deep affection and respect for cats and possesses a broad, forgiving understanding of human nature.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015), [v3 c35 P17](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0017)_

## Goals

- Obtain a yellow silk dress upon arriving in heaven  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

## History

After her daughter married and left for the mission field, Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for Nell, Honora, Cressy, and Mabel at Tabby's Place. She brought along two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted the stray cat Smudge into her care as well. She spent three winters chaperoning and keeping house for the college girls, taking joy in their company and entertaining them with her perspectives and memories. During Christmas holidays when the students returned home, she remained at Tabby's Place to tend to the house and cats. Following the girls' graduation, she took all three cats back to her home. Later, she traveled to India to investigate her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P48](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0048), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina because her father, James, drowned at sea a month prior to her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Grew up in a family with around six girls  <sub>[v3 c19 P41](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0041), [v3 c19 P42](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0042)</sub>
- Mother passed away shortly after welcoming her home without a scolding following a lost journey with Phemy Cameron  <sub>[v3 c39 P50](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0050)</sub>
- Taught cooking to her daughter before allowing her to study mathematics at university  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>
- Her only daughter married and departed for the foreign mission field  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>

## Quotes

> No. I am not an aunt to you, and I disbelieve in using names for people that do not belong to them.  <sub>[v1 c8 P13](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0013)</sub>

> It is quite an outmoded method... However, I am outmoded myself. My garments are, and naturally my views are as well.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Go out and breathe some fresh air... yet carry your umbrella with you, because I think rain is coming. My leg has rheumatism.  <sub>[v3 c25 P8](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0008)</sub>

> The four of you have been the sweetest, dearest, best girls who ever attended college as a group  <sub>[v3 c37 P13](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0013)</sub>

> I shall bring him to my house to be with Joseph and the Sarah-cat... Separating those cats after they have mastered coexisting would be a pity. Cats and people find that a difficult lesson to master.  <sub>[v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008)</sub>
